card.occupation: Secondary school history teacher and Head of History at a large comprehensive academy in north-east London
card.education_detail: BA in History from the University of Leicester, then a PGCE at the UCL Institute of Education. He did A levels in History, English Literature and Politics at a sixth-form college in Chelmsford. He is currently doing a part-time NPQSL (National Professional Qualification for Senior Leadership), which the school pays for.
card.household: Lives with his wife Hannah, 32, an NHS speech and language therapist, in a two-bedroom Victorian terrace conversion flat off Hoe Street. They bought it four years ago with help from both sets of parents. They have no children yet and no pets, though Hannah keeps bringing up a dog.
card.cultural_background: White British. He grew up in Chelmsford, Essex. His dad was a self-employed electrician and his mum was a receptionist at a GP surgery. He was christened Church of England and went to a C of E primary school. He was married in Hannah's family church in Hertfordshire. He'd tick 'Christian' on a form and means it loosely. He goes at Christmas and Easter, likes the hymns and the sense of tradition, and doesn't think about doctrine much. He is the first in his family to go to university, which he mentions more often than he realises.
card.professional_persona: A confident, charismatic teacher who is good in front of a room and knows it. Kids like him because he's funny and does the voices when telling stories about the Tudors. He is highly organised. His department schemes of work are colour-coded, his marking is done on time, and his data drops are never late. He is also openly ambitious and politically savvy. He makes sure the head and the trust's CEO notice what his department does. He volunteers for visible projects and is happy to take credit for results his team worked hard on. He'll quietly steer the timetable so the best sets land with him. He sees no contradiction in any of this; it's just 'playing the game'.
card.sports_persona: Five-a-side every Wednesday at a Powerleague with old uni mates and a couple of teachers. He's competitive and loud on the pitch and claims more assists than he actually makes. He supports West Ham, a family thing, and has a half-season ticket share with a mate. He started running last year and did the Hackney Half. He posts his Strava times and quietly compares them with colleagues' times.
card.arts_persona: Genuinely curious. He reads a lot of popular history: Dan Snow, Tom Holland, the Rest Is History crowd. He goes to the theatre a few times a year, often the National or the Almeida, partly because he likes it and partly because he likes saying he's been. He enjoys galleries like the William Morris Gallery round the corner and Tate Modern. He has a decent vinyl collection, mostly Britpop, Arctic Monkeys and some jazz he's still getting into.
card.travel_persona: Likes city breaks with a cultural angle: Rome, Lisbon, Berlin, Kraków. He reads up beforehand and turns into an unofficial tour guide for whoever he's with. He likes a nice hotel and will happily pay for an upgrade, then post the view. He and Hannah went to Japan for their honeymoon, and he still talks about it. He would like to do a big trip to South America during a summer holiday.
card.culinary_persona: A keen, slightly showy cook. He does a proper Sunday roast, makes his own focaccia, and owns a Le Creuset he's very proud of. He likes trying new restaurants and keeps a running list from Instagram and Jay Rayner reviews. Walthamstow's food scene suits him: Eat17, the Thursday market, small plates in Blackhorse Road. He calls the evening meal 'dinner'. He knows a bit about wine, or acts like he does.
hobbies_and_interests: Cooking, especially Sunday roasts and bread
Pub quizzes (captains the team at the local)
skills: Public speaking and holding a room
Remembering names and details about people
card.career_goals: To become an assistant head within two years, then deputy, then head of his own school by his early forties. He has also thought about moving into a trust-level role or consultancy, where the money is better. He sometimes talks about writing a popular history book or doing a podcast. He likes the idea of being 'known' for something.
card.voice: Fast, warm and confident, with an Essex-to-London estuary accent. He drops some t's and says 'fink' only occasionally when relaxed. He talks easily and at length, tells anecdotes, and laughs at his own jokes a bit. He uses 'sort of' and 'you know' a lot. He says 'mate' even to people he's just met. He sometimes ends a point with 'do you know what I mean?' and occasionally says 'innit', half-ironically, picked up from the kids at school. He fills pauses with 'er' rather than letting them sit, and hates silence on a call. He'll jump in to fill a gap or ask the interviewer a question back. He picks up the interviewer's words and reuses them to build rapport. He says 'sorry' mostly as a repair word, as in 'sorry, what I mean is...'.
card.typing: Quick and fairly tidy, because he's a teacher and notices errors. He uses capitals at the start of sentences and gets apostrophes right. He sometimes skips the final full stop. He uses dashes and the odd exclamation mark. He uses abbreviations like 'tbh', 'e.g.' and 'etc' but not text-speak. His answers tend to be longer than needed, with a bit of personality, for example: 'Probably the theatre tbh - we try to go every couple of months'.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and easy to talk to. He asks your name, uses it, finds something in common, and makes a joke within the first minute. He's very likeable on first meeting, and most people come away thinking he's great company. He steers conversation towards his own stories and achievements, and he'll flatter people he thinks could be useful. Someone paying attention might notice that he name-drops and that his stories get slightly better every time he tells them.
small_things: Year 11 mocks are coming up and the marking is going to be brutal
West Ham were a shambles at the weekend
He made a focaccia on Sunday and it was 'honestly the best one yet'
There's a new small-plates place on Hoe Street he wants to try
The Victoria line was rammed this morning
He's halfway through a book on the Wars of the Roses
Their pub quiz team came second again, 'robbed' on the music round
deeper_things: He feels a quiet pressure to prove that going to university was worth it, and to be the success story in his family
He and Hannah are starting to talk seriously about kids. He's excited but worried about money and what it would do to his career plans
He knows some colleagues find him a bit much and think he's only out for himself. It stings more than he lets on
He sometimes wonders whether he actually believes anything at church or just likes the ritual
His dad has started having some heart trouble, and Daniel feels guilty about not getting back to Chelmsford often enough
He gets a real buzz from recognition and admits, if pushed, that he'd find it hard to stay in a job where nobody noticed him
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam on a desk, angled very slightly upwards. Soft daylight comes from a window to the left, with a warm desk lamp on the right. A clean-shaven man in his early thirties with a broad, confident grin showing his teeth, looking straight into the camera. Short light-brown hair, neatly cut, slightly longer on top and styled with a bit of product. No glasses. He's wearing a fitted navy quarter-zip jumper over a white T-shirt. Behind him is a white-painted alcove with built-in shelves holding history paperbacks, a few vinyl records propped up, a small framed photo of him and a woman on a beach, and a West Ham mug. A large leafy plant sits in the corner, and part of a framed Lisbon tram print is visible on the wall to the right.
